Ronda Rousey Explains Why She Is The Highest Paid Fighter In The UFC

I can't dispute why she's currently the highest paid athlete in the UFC, but I gotta say interest is beginning to wane, and it's entirely not her fault.

She came onto the scene when MMA was new for women, but had already been extensively trained to become a world class athlete, in a skill that is absolutely viable to use in MMA. There is quite frankly, not very many women (if any) on the entire planet that are in her league. In all martial arts, women are typically rather scarce all things considered. Many women I trained in Thai Boxing had an extraordinarily difficult time finding any opponents, at all, to square off against. Finding someone in your state who had similar training time (not super fair to put a 10 year martial arts veteran with multiple black belts against someone who just got started 3 months ago after all), similar weight, and was going to be available to fight at fight time. Without being able to fight opponents regularly and often to temper their skills and become more proficient, it's difficult to even approach the league that she's in.

While fans love seeing knockouts, most fans don't actually like watching mismatches where one person is significantly more skilled than the other. It makes for boring, predictable fights. She's absolutely at the top of her game, and the top of her class, no question on that regard. But because she's so much more unbelievably skilled, I don't really plan on watching her fights much simply because I know the outcome in advance, and that's not what I enjoy about MMA or martial arts in general.

I will say I'd be very interested if Gina Carano came out of retirement (which she won't, and even if she did she wouldn't be at the top of her game like she used to be) for a fight against her... but I would admittedly be far more interested if she bumped herself up in weight in order to fight "Cyborg" Santos, especially with the animosity between the two of them. THAT would be a fight worth seeing. It's unfortunate, but I doubt we'll ever see a true super fight like those with Rhonda, at least not for a few more years. Hopefully she's inspiring women that it's possible to be at the top of MMA, and that it's possible for women to be fighters and encourage many more to get out there, and so that one day someone will be skilled enough to take her on and give her a true challenge.

Maybe I'm just weird. But to me, martial arts are simply beautiful. I love watching the form, the grace, the wonderful techniques, and the uncanny control of the human body. The greatest fights for me don't end in submission or knockout typically, they go the distance with two warriors battling and leaving everything in the ring. They leave both fighters bloody and tested, and those are the fights I remember. The fights where someone isn't beat to a pulp and humiliated, but the fights where the loser can be absolutely proud of their performance.
